title: Plain Language Legislation for Clarity and Accessibility
what_it_is: Plain Language Legislation for Clarity and Accessibility

sections.label: Plain language government communications
sections.summary: The Government has no plans to introduce plain language legislation, pursuing clear public communications instead through policy, the Instruction Manual, education and training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information whether the Government will consider introducing plain language legislation to ensure clarity and accessibility of Government communications, as has been passed in the United States and New Zealand.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: However, there are no plans to pursue this aim through legislation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: Our public communications policy calls for plain language, so that messages are clear and accessible for members of the public.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: The Government Instruction Manual requires all public servants to write well and speak clearly.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: Instead, we will pursue this aim through education, training, role-modelling and holding ourselves to high standards.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: The experience in other countries where legislation has been introduced suggests that our approach has merit.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: This is ongoing work, with no short cuts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: We will continue to remind ourselves and colleagues within Public Service to communicate in language that is simple, clear, precise, accurate and, ideally, concise.

sections.label: Simplified government letters, whole-of-government
sections.summary: The Government shares the intent to simplify its communications to Singaporeans as a whole-of-government effort, while ensuring precision and accuracy, with training and support for officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: So, I think my clarification is, would the Government consider implementing much more simplified communications in its letters and so on to Singaporeans, as a WOG effort.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We also do have to make sure that there is precision and accuracy in the statements.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: These are tensions that Government officers will require training and support, but I can assure Mr Perera we have the same intent.
